rows.source: HSE LOLER and lifting-equipment examination guidance
rows.verified: Lifting operations using lifting equipment must be properly planned by a competent person.

rows.source: HSE LOLER and lifting-equipment examination guidance
rows.verified: Operations should be appropriately supervised and carried out safely.

rows.source: HSE LOLER and lifting-equipment examination guidance
rows.verified: Lifting equipment should be fit for purpose, appropriate for the task and suitably marked.

rows.source: HSE LOLER and lifting-equipment examination guidance
rows.verified: Equipment should be positioned or installed to reduce risks of striking people or unintended load movement.

rows.source: HSE LOLER and lifting-equipment examination guidance
rows.verified: Many lifting systems require periodic thorough examination by a competent person.

rows.source: HSE LOLER and lifting-equipment examination guidance
rows.verified: Thorough-examination reports should record examination dates, next due dates and dangerous defects.

rows.source: HSE LOLER and lifting-equipment examination guidance
rows.verified: Serious defects must be communicated promptly and the equipment should not be used until risk is controlled.

rows.source: HSE LOLER and lifting-equipment examination guidance
rows.verified: Pre-use checks, maintenance and interim inspections may be required in addition to statutory thorough examination.

rows.source: HSE LOLER and lifting-equipment examination guidance
rows.verified: Lifting risk depends on the load, equipment, accessories, configuration, ground, environment, operator, lift plan, supervision and examination history.

rows.source: HSE LOLER and lifting-equipment examination guidance
rows.verified: A LOLER record or general guidance does not prove a specific lift is safe or establish an exact parcel-level dropped-load or overturn probability.

rows.source: HSE PUWER work-equipment guidance
rows.verified: Work equipment provided for use must be suitable for its intended purpose.

rows.source: HSE PUWER work-equipment guidance
rows.verified: Equipment must be maintained in a safe condition and in good repair.

rows.source: HSE PUWER work-equipment guidance
rows.verified: Installation-dependent equipment should be inspected after installation and before first use.

rows.source: HSE PUWER work-equipment guidance
rows.verified: Equipment exposed to deterioration that could create danger should be inspected at suitable intervals.

rows.source: HSE PUWER work-equipment guidance
rows.verified: Users, supervisors and managers need adequate information, instruction and training.

rows.source: HSE PUWER work-equipment guidance
rows.verified: Protective measures can include guards, emergency stops, isolation, markings and warning devices.

rows.source: HSE PUWER work-equipment guidance
rows.verified: Maintenance work should be planned so it can be carried out safely by competent people.

rows.source: HSE PUWER work-equipment guidance
rows.verified: Inspection frequency should reflect risk, manufacturer recommendations, industry advice and operating experience.

rows.source: HSE PUWER work-equipment guidance
rows.verified: PUWER controls depend on the specific equipment, intended use, installation, environment, deterioration mechanisms, guarding, maintenance and user competence.

rows.source: HSE PUWER work-equipment guidance
rows.verified: General PUWER evidence does not establish the current condition or legal compliance of equipment at an individual parcel.
